name: Nzambi Mpungu
role: Kongo creator and source of life
symbols: the four movements of the day
fun_fact: In Kikongo, Nzambi is the ordinary word for God, a usage shaped by centuries of Christian translation as well as older Kongo tradition.

name: Mwindo
role: Nyanga hero born walking and talking
fun_fact: Mwindo's epic is performed at night by a single bard, and the hero's boasts are played for laughter as much as awe.

name: Chameleon
role: Slow messenger who carries the news of life
fun_fact: The chameleon's slow walk is the whole plot: in many southern African versions, death enters the world because the news arrived late.

name: Unkulunkulu
fun_fact: His name means 'the very great old one', and Zulu Christians later used it for God, much as missionaries used Nzambi in Kongo.

name: Mbidi Kiluwe
role: Luba culture hero who brought sacred kingship
fun_fact: Mbidi returned east after fathering Kalala Ilunga, and Luba royal tradition later traced the kings' legitimacy to that crossing of the water.

name: Kalala Ilunga
role: First king of the Luba royal line
fun_fact: His defeat of Nkongolo is recited by the Mbudye society as a charter of Luba kingship rather than as a simple war story.

name: Kintu
fun_fact: Kintu is also remembered as an early king of Buganda, so the first man and the first monarch share a name.

name: Nambi
role: Daughter of Gulu who marries Kintu
fun_fact: Nambi's brother is Walumbe, Death, so her marriage brings both the first family and the first funeral to earth.

name: Gulu
role: Sky lord and father of Nambi
fun_fact: Gulu is also called Mugulu, and his tests are the moral hinge of the Kintu story.

name: Modjadji
fun_fact: The title is hereditary through women, and the queenship continues in Limpopo today, so it is a living office rather than a figure from an ancient text.
